title: Do VLMs Align Better with Humans than LLMs Do during Natural Reading?
abstract: arXiv:2605.28818v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly useful computational models of human language processing, yet it remains open whether vision--language learning is associated with more human-like text representations during natural reading. We address this question by comparing matched LLM and vision--language model (VLM) pairs under strictly text-only input and evaluating alignment with human brain activity (whole-cortex fMRI) and reading behavior (synchronized regressive saccades). Across evaluated pairs, we identify a selective, rather than global, pattern in human--model alignment. translated_title: 视觉语言模型在自然阅读中是否比大语言模型更贴近人类？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）已成为日益有用的人类语言处理计算模型，但视觉语言学习是否能在自然阅读过程中产生更接近人类的文本表征，仍是一个悬而未决的问题。我们通过在严格纯文本输入条件下比较匹配的大语言模型与视觉语言模型（VLM）对，并评估其与人类大脑活动（全皮层fMRI）及阅读行为（同步回视性眼跳）的对齐程度来回答这一问题。在所评估的模型对中，我们发现人-模型对齐呈现出选择性而非全局性的模式。在第一方持续预训练的模型对（Qwen2和DeepSeek）中，视觉语言模型更准确地预测了人类的回视性眼跳，同时在全皮层fMRI对齐上与匹配的大语言模型表现出实际等同性；而LoRA适配的模型对（Mistral/Idefics2）则未显示出差异。然而，句子层面的fMRI分析揭示了视觉语言模型日益增长的优势。
tldr: 本研究在纯文本输入下比较匹配的LLM与VLM对，发现视觉语言训练带来的优势是选择性的——VLM在预测人类回视眼跳上更准确，并在fMRI对齐上与LLM相当甚至日益占优，表明视觉语言学习能带来更接近人类的文本表征。
en_tdlr: Comparing matched LLM and VLM pairs under strictly text-only input, this study finds that vision-language training yields selective human-alignment advantages—VLMs better predict human regressive saccades and show equivalent or growing fMRI alignment—indicating more human-like text representations during natural reading.
